cycle1.result: Audio-recorded audits showed a precisely executed checklist 73.6% of the time, compared with a previously reported compliance rate of 97.6%.

audits.intervention: not reported
audits.other_findings: Fidelity was highest in pre-anaesthesia and pre-incision sections and lowest in the post-procedure section; positive staff attitudes on patient safety rose by 11% from baseline.
audits.citation: Salgado D, Barber KR, Danic M. Objective Assessment of Checklist Fidelity Using Digital Audio Recording and a Standardized Scoring System Audit. J Patient Saf. 2019;15(3):260-266. doi:10.1097/pts.0000000000000306. PMID: 27811595.

audits.title: A quality improvement initiative using peer audit and feedback to improve compliance.
audits.standard: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist standard items (four at Sign In, five at Team Time Out, two at Sign Out); at least 30 observations per hospital
audits.setting: National pilot programme, 11 hospitals with 14 sites

cycle1.result: On average 86% of standard items read out; Sign Out items 60% and 74%; all team members stopped work in 61%; items read from checklist in 71%; visual checks in 41%; verbal confirmation 76%.

audits.intervention: Peer observation with immediate peer feedback (feedback given in 79% of observations).
audits.other_findings: Surgical teams reacted positively to peer feedback in 64%; Sign Out and visual checks were main areas for improvement.
audits.citation: Fridrich A, Imhof A, Staender S, Brenni M, Schwappach D. A quality improvement initiative using peer audit and feedback to improve compliance. Int J Qual Health Care. 2022;34(3):mzac058. doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzac058. PMID: 35770658.

audits.title: Multicenter audit of operating room staff compliance with the surgical safety checklist: a cross-sectional study from a low- and middle-income country.
audits.standard: WHO surgical safety checklist
audits.setting: One governmental and one non-governmental hospital

cycle1.result: Checklist fully completed 27.9%, partially 43.2%, blank 28.8%

audits.intervention: not reported
audits.other_findings: Compliance associated with age, sex and type of surgery; staff attitudes were positive. Re-audits recommended.
audits.citation: Yaseen SJ, Taha S, Alkaiyat A, Zyoud SH. Multicenter audit of operating room staff compliance with the surgical safety checklist: a cross-sectional study from a low- and middle-income country. BMC Health Serv Res. 2025;25(1):103. doi:10.1186/s12913-025-12288-6. PMID: 39828673.

audits.title: Phased implementation of surgical safety care bundle in a multispecialty, tertiary care teaching hospital: a quality improvement project.
audits.standard: WHO Safe Surgery Saves Lives: surgical safety checklist, consent, site marking and sponge count
audits.setting: Christian Medical College and Hospital Vellore, multispecialty tertiary teaching hospital

cycle1.result: Checklist use 65%; general consent availability 56%; sponge count documentation below 80%

audits.intervention: Phased surgical care safety bundle, specialised consents, site marking, sponge count protocol and repeated education

cycle2.result: Checklist use 97%; specialised consent compliance 99%; site marking 95%; sponge count above 90%

audits.other_findings: Checklist use 70% in 2014 and 86% in 2016; site marking baseline 74% in 2017. No never events after 2019 and more near-miss reporting.
audits.citation: Joselyn AS, Joseph L, Loganathan A, Ebenezer J, Abraham S, Ranjan M. Phased implementation of surgical safety care bundle in a multispecialty, tertiary care teaching hospital: a quality improvement project.
